reason: I want to build the skin's surface, and joining surface cells seems relevant to a protective layer.
expectation: I expect the junctions to connect the surface cells into a sheet, though I don't know how complete the layer will be.

alternatives.reason: The support cells and fibers also seem useful for the skin, but I chose to start with its outer surface.

effect: The junctions made a continuous sheet, so I can now add its tougher outer layer.
reaction: That matched my expectation and clarified why the cells need connections.
reason: Adding the tough outer layer seems like the next step toward a skin boundary that resists wear.
expectation: I expect a more protective surface layer, though it may still need support underneath.

alternatives.reason: The fibers and support cells also seem relevant, but I want to finish building the surface first.

effect: The surface barrier now resists wear and unwanted passage, and I learned that deeper living cells replace its dead outer cells. It still appears to need support.
reaction: The replaceable dead outer cells were a useful surprise.
reason: Connective fibers and skin support cells seem likely to form the supporting tissue beneath the barrier.
expectation: I expect a supportive skin layer that can be joined to the surface barrier.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the arm to its supply network also seems useful, but building the skin is the current goal.

effect: The fibers and support cells formed a deeper skin layer, so I can now join it to the surface barrier.
reaction: The reminder that tissue includes material outside cells was useful.
reason: Joining the two layers should advance the goal of making a layered skin model.
expectation: I expect a skin model combining the protective surface with its supporting layer.

alternatives.reason: The arm needs its supply network, but the skin layers are ready to join now.

effect: The surface barrier and supporting layer now form layered skin; I can add sensory endings next.
reaction: The result fit my expectation and brought the two layers' roles together.
reason: Adding sensory endings should give the skin a way to detect contact.
expectation: I expect skin that can sense touch, though I don't yet know how its signals connect to the arm.

alternatives.reason: The arm also needs the supply network, but the sensory endings are ready to add to the skin.

effect: The skin can now report contact through nerve pathways, and the new goal calls for joining it with supply and control.
reaction: It is useful to see skin serving as both a barrier and a source of information.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect the arm to the supplies its cells need.
expectation: I expect an arm connected to the body supply network; it may still need the sensitive skin added.

effect: The arm now has a continuing blood supply alongside nervous control, so it is ready to receive the skin.
reaction: The distinction between supplying and directing the same action brought the earlier systems together.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should join the skin's protection and sensation to the supplied arm.
expectation: I expect a protected, sensitive arm connected to its supply and control systems.

effect: The arm, skin, supply routes and control systems now form a living body model, and the remaining goal is to lift and hold the glass.
reaction: Bringing the systems together made their cooperation clearer; the reminder that upkeep continues was useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly addresses the new goal.
expectation: I expect the model to lift the glass and hold it still, using coordinated muscle pulls and continuing supplies.

effect: The completed model shows that holding the glass still requires continuing muscle activity, signals, supplies and skin maintenance.
reaction: The idea that stillness still takes work was a satisfying connection to the original task.

mostWorthwhile.text: Lifting and holding the glass brought the systems together in a familiar action and showed why the cells must keep working.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the two skin layers was predictable after building them, though it clarified their different roles.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the outermost skin cells are dead and are continually replaced by living cells deeper down.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary; even the only available combinations had purposes connected to the goals.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter explored a similarly concrete body function. The connections were interesting, although several steps were predictable.
